print_errors.note: Line 2: the lam of الوَهَّابِ has no sukun (checked at 2000 dpi), but عَبْدِ الْوَهَّابِ (line 2) and بِاسْمِكَ الْوَهَّابِ (line 4) both have one. Kept as printed.
No fatha on the jim of رَجاءَ (checked at 1000 dpi). Kept as printed.
No damma on the kaf (checked at 3000 dpi). In the same line, وَالْفُهُوم؛ has no vowel on its final mim. Both kept as printed.
الْوجُودِ has no damma on the first waw, and الشُّهودِ has no damma on the ha (checked at 1800-2400 dpi). Kept as printed.
The ط has no sukun and the ها has no fatha. Only the ت carries a fatha (checked at 2400 dpi). Kept as printed.
The last line's بِقَوْلك has no kasra on the lam and no fatha on the kaf (checked at 2400 dpi). The earlier بِقَوْلِكَ on the same page (line 9) has both. Kept as printed.

notes:
Markers: p112 ends with a complete prayer («…عَطَاءَ السُّعَدَاءِ.») and has no footnotes. p113, p114, p115 and p116 each start a new numbered item (١٧-، ١٩-، ٢١/٢٢-، ٢٥/٢٦-), so no page gets '+'. There is no (تابع). p116 ends inside the Quran quote of al-Ma'ida 8 («﴿ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ»), which continues on p117. I closed it with ﴾ at the end of p116, as in b27/b28, because validate.py needs balanced brackets on each line, so p117 should be '+' and reopen ﴿.

Red and bold: red is only the divine Name, found by RGB pixel analysis. Both names are red in ٢٧/٢٨ (سَمِيعُ، بَصِيرُ) and ٢٩/٣٠ (حَكَمُ، عَدْلُ). Only the first name is red in ٢١/٢٢ (قَابِضُ), ٢٣/٢٤ (خَافِضَ) and ٢٥/٢٦ (مُعِزَّ). The second name there is black: بَاسِطُ is regular weight, but رَافِعَ (p115) and مُذِلَّ (p116) are clearly set in the heavier name font (stroke median 15-18 px against 10-13 px for nearby words at 1200 dpi). I marked those two **…**. The black يَا between red names, and the commas after them, are outside the markers. In the p114 footnote the two hadith texts are bold. The guillemets are light, so they stay outside the **. The main-text hadith «أَنَا أَعْلَمُكُمْ…» is regular weight.

Item numbers like ٢١/٢٢- were ordered from pixel column runs: the right-hand number comes first. Ink gaps show no space after the slash. Footnote refs (١/١٣) and (٧/١٤٢) were measured the same way: the gaps around the slash equal the digits' own side-bearings, so no space.

The name الله with a printed case vowel (صَلَّى اللهُ ×2; footnote «وَاللهِ…» and «…للهِ») is written fully vowelled, اللَّهُ / وَاللَّهِ / للَّهِ, as in b27/b28. Where only the font ligature is printed (بِالله and لله» in the text; بِالله أَنَا in the footnote) it is written plain.

The kasra under the lam-alif of وَالِاسْتِقَامَةِ (p115) is encoded on the lam, as in b28. Final ى outside Quran is plain (عَلَى، يَخْشَى، حَتَّى، وَمَعْنًى، الضحى، صَلَّى، أَتَعَالَى، أَرَى، النَّجْوَى). يَا رَحْمَنُ (p116) has a slanted fatha on the mim, not a dagger alif (2000 dpi).

Partial vowelling kept as printed, for example: وبَارِكْ, ونُعْمَاكَ, الْأَكْوانَ (p114, no fatha on waw; p115 has الْأَكْوَانَ with it), وَالْإِيقانِ (an apparent fatha over its lam-alif is the kasra of الفتاح's ح from the line above), وراثةِ, الإِحْسَانِ (no sukun on lam), يُقَرِّبُنا, والرِّزْقِ, تَرْفَعُني and تُعِزُّني (no kasra on nun, unlike تَرْزُقُنِي), ومَنْ, وتُذِلُّ, وأَعْدَائِي, مِنْهُم, بِكفايَتِكَ, غَوايةٍ, عَزيزُ, ويَا (p116 ٢٧/٢٨).

Combined marks over الـ were read at 2400-3000 dpi: الْمَعَارِفِ and الْمَعْبُودِ are sukun+fatha. حَالَتَيِ has a separate kasra under the ya, above the shadda+kasra of the next line's كُلِّ.

Quran: the encoding follows Tanzil. ٱلسَّآئِلَ (93:10) is drawn with the hamza under the tooth and a kasra, and is encoded ئِ as in Tanzil, matching b28's وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ. The silent alifs in تُوَلُّوا۟ and ٱعْدِلُوا۟ are round zeros (۟). Waqf ۚ is printed on رَحْمَةً (3:8) and ءَايَٰتِنَآ (17:1). Isra 1 is printed with «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ» inserted in ordinary type between هُوَ and ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ, so it is two ﴿…﴾ spans. scripts/quran.py flags only the quote-final waqf signs of 2:115 (ۚ) and 16:53 (ۖ). They are not printed (the bracket follows ٱللَّهِ directly) and were not added.

Spacing: «(٨)﴾[آل عمران: ٨]» on p113 is printed glued (26 px at 1000 dpi, the same as b16's glued cases), so it is kept glued. My b28 wrote the similar p112 case with a space, so the reconciler should pick one form. The other ﴾ [ cases are clearly spaced (about 60 px), or split by a line break.
